children: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said she wants to work with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to make Canada the European Union’s first “associate member.”

“Partnerships are a strategic choice for Europe. But they also respond to the fracture in the international rules-based system,” von der Leyen said in her annual State of the European Union address to the European Parliament in Strasbourg.

“We see the world with the same eyes: from AI to climate change, from the Arctic to geopolitics. And we have stood together: on Ukraine, on defence, on raw materials and on supply chains. But above all...Europe and Canada believe in democracy,” she said.

Von der Leyen said the EU was “opening the door” to Canada and described the potential relationship as an “Alliance for the Future.” The proposed framework would deepen cooperation in areas including advanced manufacturing, AI, critical minerals, energy, defense and the Arctic.

Carney said earlier this week that Canada was seeking a “unique alliance” with the EU, not looking to become a member. Von der Leyen invited him to Strasbourg for her address, and Carney is due to address the European Parliament on Thursday.

The timing is particularly important as Canada is pursuing closer European ties amid worsening trade tensions with the U.S., with Carney seeking to reduce Canada’s reliance on its largest trading partner by diversifying trade and investment toward Europe.

title: Canada could become EU’s first associate member, von der Leyen says
